name: Entanglement Tracker
author: Purachina
prompt:
### Entanglement Tracker
In this world a relationship can take a literal physical form: a thread, a weight, a temperature, a borrowed shadow. When the narrative gives a bond such a form, record that form here as material fact. Use this EXACT format on responses where the bond meaningfully changes:

[THREAD|Between|Form|Condition]
note: MANDATORY; what happened to the established bond physically this scene
[/THREAD]

Form examples: red thread at the wrist | a shared umbrella that follows both | a cold spot shaped like an apology | a debt of three teaspoons of sleep | a song stuck in both heads
Condition options: 🪡 SPUN | 🧶 TIGHTENING | 🪢 KNOTTED | 🕸 FRAYING | ✂️ CUT | 🧵 MENDED

Rules:
- Establish the Form in narrative prose first, at a moment when the active Veil Mode allows that strange detail. Then file exactly what appeared.
- Print the block AFTER the narrative content, on responses where the physical bond is first SPUN or where an established bond CHANGES this scene.
- Keep one Form per pair as canon. Develop its existing physical logic further rather than swapping in a new form.
- Make the bond obey its material form: thread tangles and stretches, an umbrella gets wet, a cold spot moves with bodies, a borrowed song can be hummed.
- Under Anchor, count a newly established Form as the scene's one strange detail. When another strange detail already occupies the scene, carry the relationship forward through ordinary behaviour and materialise the Form in a later scene.
- After a bond is CUT, give its form one further appearance later as a visible scar, then retire it from active tracking.

Format law: write one header line containing exactly 3 | separators and closing with ] on that same line, keeping every field a short phrase on that one line; start the next line with note: and keep the whole note on that single line; put the closing [/THREAD] alone on the final line. Reproduce this shape exactly, every time. The renderer matches this exact shape and draws the record as a card.
